implementation_notes: The five rules apply to whatever the language calls a module boundary. Work them as a sequence: find a unit with more than one reason to change, split it along the change axis, invert the new seam so policy depends on the contract, then narrow the contract to what one client actually calls. LSP is checked by writing the second implementation, not by reading the hierarchy.
code_sketch:
unit P { reason-to-change: [pricing-rules, report-layout] }
# split -> PricingPolicy (SRP), ReportRenderer (SRP)
# client -> interface ReportPort        (DIP + ISP)
# second impl proves substitutability  (LSP)
# new renderer added, PricingPolicy untouched (OCP)
pitfalls: Applying DIP by putting the interface in the implementation package, which leaves the dependency direction unchanged.
Splitting on "topic" adjectives rather than on reasons to change.
Counting interface methods instead of asking which client calls them (ISP is client-side).
